pathway.title: GENESIS ENERGY LP — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The first finding is liquidity and maturities. Genesis ended the third quarter of 2026 with USD 41.477 million of unrestricted cash and USD 894.4 million of revolver availability, no revolver borrowings, and no debt maturing until the 8.250% notes of USD 600.0 million fall due on January 15, 2029 [CP-1, Chart data: liquidity and debt maturities]. The mechanism is the March 2026 refinancing, which replaced the 2028 notes with USD 750.0 million of 2034 notes and extended the revolver to March 4, 2031 [CP-1A, Transaction summary]. The implication is that default risk from refinancing in the next two years is low; the condition is that revolver availability is stated as subject to covenant compliance.

The second finding is that leverage has not fallen. Total debt principal was USD 3,249.5 million at September 30, 2026 against USD 3,085.760 million at December 31, 2025, and computed total debt to EBITDA was 5.18x on a last-twelve-months basis against 5.74x for FY2025, with net debt to EBITDA of 5.12x [CP-1, Chart data: leverage]. The ratio improved because EBITDA grew, not because debt fell: the debt increase came from the 2034 notes, the AR Facility of USD 99.5 million and USD 221.6 million of preferred unit purchases funded partly by debt [CP-1A, Transaction summary]. The implication is that the partnership is trading junior, higher-cost capital for senior debt, which lowers cash costs but raises the claims ahead of equity and leaves leverage tolerance dependent on EBITDA.

The third finding is debt service capacity. EBITDA to cash interest was 2.36x on a last-twelve-months basis and 1.90x for FY2025, and the notes alone carry a run-rate coupon of USD 247.625 million a year, equal to 39.5% of last-twelve-months computed EBITDA of USD 626.898 million [CP-1, Chart data: interest cover; Calculations]. The mechanism is high-coupon unsecured notes against a business whose margin is concentrated in offshore pipelines. The implication is that a modest EBITDA shortfall consumes interest cover quickly; the covenant minimum of 2.00x through December 31, 2026 rising to 2.15x in 2027 is not reported by management and cannot be tested here.

The fourth finding is covenant headroom. Management reports a covenant leverage ratio of 5.03x against a 5.75x maximum through December 31, 2027, and the release's own inputs imply an EBITDA cushion of USD 76.041 million or 12.5% [CP-1, Covenants and definitions review]. The mechanism is that covenant EBITDA includes pro forma adjustments of USD 11.405 million and covenant debt excludes the AR Facility; an illustrative fall of about 9.9% in computed EBITDA would lift computed leverage to 5.75x (Calculations; not a covenant test because the bases differ). The implication is that headroom is adequate today but is the variable that governs revolver access, and it cannot be verified without the executed credit agreement.

The fifth finding is business risk. Offshore pipelines produced 67.7% of nine-month 2026 Segment Margin under life-of-lease and minimum-volume arrangements, and in the third quarter Shenandoah volumes were below the minimum so only the minimum was recognized; management expects Adjusted EBITDA near or below the low end of guidance [CP-1A, Credit translations]. The mechanism is that minimum volume commitments floor margin but cap upside when third-party wells underperform, and Gulf weather adds interruption risk (about four days of disruption in October 2026). The implication is that the contracted base supports debt service while growth depends on producers.

The sixth finding is cash conversion. Nine-month 2026 operating cash flow of USD 340.898 million included a working capital inflow of USD 58.619 million, and cash after capital payments and distributions was USD 101.661 million, before USD 221.594 million of preferred unit redemptions [CP-1, Credit narrative by dimension]. The mechanism is crude marketing, which moves receivables and payables together, with receivables partly financed through the AR Facility. The implication is that reported cash flow overstates the underlying run-rate and that free cash after distributions is small relative to debt, so deleveraging depends on EBITDA growth or asset sales rather than free cash flow.

runs.text: Strengths. First, contracted and fee-based offshore cash flow: pipelines under life-of-lease commitments and minimum volume commitments provided 67.7% of nine-month 2026 Segment Margin (Documentary Fact; CP-1A Company and operating model). Second, liquidity and maturity profile: USD 894.4 million of revolver availability, USD 41.477 million of cash and no maturity before January 2029 (Documentary Fact; CP-1). Third, diversified customers and assets: no customer above 10% of 2025 revenue, a marine fleet mostly on time charters and a sulfur services business with refinery contracts (Documentary Fact; CP-1A). Fourth, lower funding costs from the 2026 actions: the 2034 notes carry a lower coupon than the retired 2028 notes and the AR Facility prices at SOFR plus 1.375%, while repurchased preferred units carried an annual coupon of 11.24% (Documentary Fact; CP-1A Transaction summary). Management describes these steps as having eliminated near-term refinancing risk, which is Management Language and is not adopted here.

Weaknesses. First, leverage and cover: 5.18x total debt to EBITDA and 2.36x EBITDA to cash interest, with debt higher than at year end (Documentary Fact for the figures; Analyst Interpretation for the reading). Second, earnings concentration and volume risk: offshore volumes depend on third-party producers, Shenandoah was at the minimum in Q3 2026 and management guides to the low end of the range (Documentary Fact; Management Language for the guidance). Third, control and capital allocation: Class B units elect the board and a family group holds 77% of them, and the partnership bought back preferred units with debt while raising common distributions (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation for the creditor reading). Fourth, definition and documentation gaps: the management covenant ratio uses a different debt and EBITDA perimeter and the executed credit documents are not supplied (Insufficient Information for covenant headroom verification).

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The transactions that matter to a creditor all sit between February 2025 and September 2026 and share one purpose, stated in the 10-K strategy as "reducing debt in absolute terms and opportunistically redeeming our high-cost Class A Convertible Preferred Units". On February 28, 2025 the partnership completed the sale of the Alkali Business for a gross purchase price of $1.425 billion; the buyer assumed $413.4 million of 5.875% senior secured notes due 2042, and the proceeds paid down the revolver, bought 7,416,196 preferred units at $35.40 on March 6, 2025 and redeemed the remaining $406.2 million of the 8.000% notes due 2027 on April 3, 2025. That sale is why 2025 comparatives separate discontinued operations. On March 4, 2026 the partnership issued $750.0 million of 6.750% senior unsecured notes due March 15, 2034 with net proceeds of about $735.9 million, used to buy $416.1 million of the 7.750% notes due 2028 in a tender and to redeem the remaining $263.3 million on March 22, 2026. The same day it entered the Eighth Amended and Restated Credit Agreement, raising the revolver from $800 million to $900 million and moving expiry to March 4, 2031, with springing earlier maturities if more than $150 million of the 2029 notes remain outstanding on October 16, 2028 or more than $150 million of the 2030 notes on January 14, 2030. The mechanics are credit-relevant: the new notes carry a lower coupon than the retired notes (calculated 50.625 million a year on 750.0 million against 52.650 million a year on 679.360 million) but 70.640 million more principal, and the 2028 wall was replaced by a 2034 maturity. Preferred purchases in 2026 were 741,620 units on February 3 at $33.71 for $25.0 million, 3,263,127 units on March 6 at $34.38 for $112.2 million and 2,454,445 units on June 8 at $34.38 for $84.4 million, a total of 6,459,192 units for $221.6 million (calculated), funded, according to the 10-Q, by the remaining 2034 note proceeds, operating cash flow and revolver borrowings (the March purchase) and by the $95.0 million proceeds of the June 3, 2026 sale of non-core natural gas pipeline and platform assets (the June purchase), while the funding of the February purchase is not stated; the repurchased units carried distributions of $3.7892 per unit a year, or about $24.5 million a year in total (calculated), at an annual coupon of 11.24%. On June 26, 2026 the partnership entered a three-year $99.5 million AR Facility at SOFR plus 1.375%, through a bankruptcy-remote subsidiary that is not a guarantor; it is fully drawn. Debt service and liquidity effects are in CP-1: total debt principal rose to $3,249.5 million, no maturity falls before January 15, 2029, and revolver availability was $894.4 million at September 30, 2026. The creditor mechanics are therefore a lower cost of capital and a longer maturity profile at the price of more senior debt: the preferred units are equity (mezzanine) that ranks senior only to the common units, so each purchase exchanges junior capital for senior debt. Management says these steps "eliminated any near-term refinancing risk"; that is management language, and the revolver's springing maturities and covenants remain. No sponsor transaction, dividend recapitalization or non-pro-rata exchange appears in the sources; the seller of the repurchased preferred units is described only as one of the holders and is not named.

fields.value: The financial base is usable for the requested work, with limitations. Audited FY2025 statements, three unaudited 2026 interim statements and three releases give consistent continuing-operations figures for the consolidated partnership, and every figure in the tables below is printed in, or calculated from, those sources. On a computed basis (operating income plus depreciation and amortization plus equity in earnings, less the 2026 asset-sale gain) LTM Q3 2026 EBITDA is 626.898 US$m, total debt to EBITDA is 5.18x, net debt to EBITDA is 5.12x and EBITDA to cash interest paid is 2.36x. Management reports a covenant leverage ratio of 5.03x, which uses a different debt and EBITDA perimeter. The two bases must not be mixed: the computed basis is consolidated and gross of noncontrolling interests, while management's Adjusted EBITDA is net to Genesis' ownership. Funded debt is $3,150.000 million of senior unsecured notes plus a $99.500 million AR Facility, with no revolver borrowings at September 30, 2026. Liquidity at that date is $41.477 million of unrestricted cash plus $894.4 million of revolver availability, subject to covenant compliance. Limitations that restrict conclusions: the credit agreement and indentures are not supplied; FY2025 adjusted EBITDA and a covenant ratio at December 31, 2025 are not printed; FY2025 cash flows are consolidated and include the discontinued Alkali Business for January and February 2025; and the Q3 10-Q and the Q3 release disagree on two inputs to the management leverage ratio.

Evidence: operating cash flow of 340.898 US$m in nine months of 2026 against 142.044 in 2025, with working capital contributing +58.619 against (90.379); receivables rose to 1,053.898 from 608.221 and payables to 927.687 from 490.712 (10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl pages:2, 5). Mechanic: the 10-Q says "our accounts receivable and accounts payable generally move in tandem" (10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl page:50), so the rise in both is consistent with higher crude marketing activity; the AR Facility of 99.500 is drawn against receivables. Operating cash flow excluding the working capital line is 282.279 (calculated). After capital payments of 84.996, common distributions of 68.531, preferred distributions of 38.946 and net noncontrolling distributions of 46.764, free cash is 101.661 US$m (calculated), before the 221.594 US$m preferred redemptions. Implication: reported cash generation is partly timing and the 2025 comparison includes the Alkali Business; underlying free cash after distributions is positive but small relative to debt.

Evidence: 41.477 US$m unrestricted cash and 894.4 US$m revolver availability (total 935.877, calculated), no revolver borrowings, letters of credit of 5.6 against a 50 allowance, AR Facility fully drawn at 99.5 limit. Mechanic: availability is "subject to compliance with covenants" and the revolver has springing maturities tied to the 2029 and 2030 notes. Implication: ample near-term liquidity, but access is conditional on the leverage test; no debt matures before January 15, 2029.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Genesis Energy, L.P. is a Delaware master limited partnership that earns most of its margin from fee-based midstream services in the Gulf of America and the Gulf Coast: offshore crude oil and natural gas pipelines, a Jones Act marine fleet, and onshore refinery-linked pipelines, terminals and sulfur removal. The view for a creditor is mixed but constructive on durability. Offshore pipelines operate under life-of-lease commitments and, for the Shenandoah development, contractual minimum volume commitments on the 100% owned SYNC Pipeline and the 64% owned CHOPS Pipeline; marine is mostly time charters; onshore marketing is back-to-back and adds revenue with little margin. Counter-evidence is also on the page: in Q3 2026 Shenandoah volumes were below the minimum, management says production shortfalls continue into early 2027 and that 2026 Adjusted EBITDA will likely be near or below the low end of guidance. The transaction record is dominated by deliberate balance-sheet repositioning: the 2025 sale of the Alkali Business, the March 2026 refinancing into 2034 notes and a new revolver, the June 2026 asset sale, a new receivables facility and repeated purchases of high-cost preferred units. Ownership and control are concentrated: Class B common units elect the board, and the preferred units carry senior distribution and liquidation rights. Facts are tagged below as Documentary Fact, Management Language, Analyst Interpretation or Insufficient Information.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The transactions that matter to a creditor all sit between February 2025 and September 2026 and share one purpose, stated in the 10-K strategy as "reducing debt in absolute terms and opportunistically redeeming our high-cost Class A Convertible Preferred Units". On February 28, 2025 the partnership completed the sale of the Alkali Business for a gross purchase price of $1.425 billion; the buyer assumed $413.4 million of 5.875% senior secured notes due 2042, and the proceeds paid down the revolver, bought 7,416,196 preferred units at $35.40 on March 6, 2025 and redeemed the remaining $406.2 million of the 8.000% notes due 2027 on April 3, 2025. That sale is why 2025 comparatives separate discontinued operations. On March 4, 2026 the partnership issued $750.0 million of 6.750% senior unsecured notes due March 15, 2034 with net proceeds of about $735.9 million, used to buy $416.1 million of the 7.750% notes due 2028 in a tender and to redeem the remaining $263.3 million on March 22, 2026. The same day it entered the Eighth Amended and Restated Credit Agreement, raising the revolver from $800 million to $900 million and moving expiry to March 4, 2031, with springing earlier maturities if more than $150 million of the 2029 notes remain outstanding on October 16, 2028 or more than $150 million of the 2030 notes on January 14, 2030. The mechanics are credit-relevant: the new notes carry a lower coupon than the retired notes (calculated 50.625 million a year on 750.0 million against 52.650 million a year on 679.360 million) but 70.640 million more principal, and the 2028 wall was replaced by a 2034 maturity. Preferred purchases in 2026 were 741,620 units on February 3 at $33.71 for $25.0 million, 3,263,127 units on March 6 at $34.38 for $112.2 million and 2,454,445 units on June 8 at $34.38 for $84.4 million, a total of 6,459,192 units for $221.6 million (calculated), funded, according to the 10-Q, by the remaining 2034 note proceeds, operating cash flow and revolver borrowings (the March purchase) and by the $95.0 million proceeds of the June 3, 2026 sale of non-core natural gas pipeline and platform assets (the June purchase), while the funding of the February purchase is not stated; the repurchased units carried distributions of $3.7892 per unit a year, or about $24.5 million a year in total (calculated), at an annual coupon of 11.24%. On June 26, 2026 the partnership entered a three-year $99.5 million AR Facility at SOFR plus 1.375%, through a bankruptcy-remote subsidiary that is not a guarantor; it is fully drawn. Debt service and liquidity effects are in CP-1: total debt principal rose to $3,249.5 million, no maturity falls before January 15, 2029, and revolver availability was $894.4 million at September 30, 2026. The creditor mechanics are therefore a lower cost of capital and a longer maturity profile at the price of more senior debt: the preferred units are equity (mezzanine) that ranks senior only to the common units, so each purchase exchanges junior capital for senior debt. Management says these steps "eliminated any near-term refinancing risk"; that is management language, and the revolver's springing maturities and covenants remain. No sponsor transaction, dividend recapitalization or non-pro-rata exchange appears in the sources; the seller of the repurchased preferred units is described only as one of the holders and is not named.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership is held through publicly traded Class A common units, a small class of Class B common units with exclusive right to elect the board, and the preferred units. The general partner owns a non-economic interest and has "sole responsibility for conducting our business and managing our operations" (10-K_2025-12-31_gel-20251231.htm.jsonl page:8), so unitholder-level checks depend on the Class B holders. Documented legal capacity: the partnership agreement authorizes the general partner to issue additional limited partner interests (10-K_2025-12-31_gel-20251231.htm.jsonl page:200), and Class B transfers do not need unitholder consent (10-K_2025-12-31_gel-20251231.htm.jsonl page:65). Willingness, shown by documented actions only: distributions to common units rose from 0.165 to 0.20 per unit, a 21.2% increase (calculated) matching the release's "increase of approximately 21%" for Q3 2026 against Q3 2025 (EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl page:2), and 250,000 units were repurchased in 2026 at about $14.57 each for $3.6 million (10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl page:19). Feasibility: leverage, cover and liquidity are in CP-1. Tag: Neutral or Mixed. Reasoning: documented actions include deleveraging with asset-sale proceeds in 2025, but 2026 preferred purchases were partly debt-funded, common unit repurchases restarted in 2026 and distributions rose while total debt rose, and there is no evidence of priming, drop-downs or non-pro-rata exchanges. Evidence quality: High (primary, dated, issuer-specific) for actions; Low for intent.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Genesis Energy, L.P. is a leveraged but liquid Gulf of America midstream credit: contracted offshore pipeline cash flows and a refinanced maturity profile support its debt service, while leverage of 5.18x and interest cover of 2.36x leave limited room for error. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 41.477 million of cash and USD 894.4 million of undrawn revolver, with no maturity before January 2029. The weakest point is that debt rose to USD 3,249.5 million in 2026 as preferred units were bought back, and that offshore volumes at Shenandoah were below the contractual minimum in the third quarter. Producer volumes, covenant headroom and the 2029 refinancing decide the outcome.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first finding is liquidity and maturities. Genesis ended the third quarter of 2026 with USD 41.477 million of unrestricted cash and USD 894.4 million of revolver availability, no revolver borrowings, and no debt maturing until the 8.250% notes of USD 600.0 million fall due on January 15, 2029 [CP-1, Chart data: liquidity and debt maturities]. The mechanism is the March 2026 refinancing, which replaced the 2028 notes with USD 750.0 million of 2034 notes and extended the revolver to March 4, 2031 [CP-1A, Transaction summary]. The implication is that default risk from refinancing in the next two years is low; the condition is that revolver availability is stated as subject to covenant compliance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second finding is that leverage has not fallen. Total debt principal was USD 3,249.5 million at September 30, 2026 against USD 3,085.760 million at December 31, 2025, and computed total debt to EBITDA was 5.18x on a last-twelve-months basis against 5.74x for FY2025, with net debt to EBITDA of 5.12x [CP-1, Chart data: leverage]. The ratio improved because EBITDA grew, not because debt fell: the debt increase came from the 2034 notes, the AR Facility of USD 99.5 million and USD 221.6 million of preferred unit purchases funded partly by debt [CP-1A, Transaction summary]. The implication is that the partnership is trading junior, higher-cost capital for senior debt, which lowers cash costs but raises the claims ahead of equity and leaves leverage tolerance dependent on EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third finding is debt service capacity. EBITDA to cash interest was 2.36x on a last-twelve-months basis and 1.90x for FY2025, and the notes alone carry a run-rate coupon of USD 247.625 million a year, equal to 39.5% of last-twelve-months computed EBITDA of USD 626.898 million [CP-1, Chart data: interest cover; Calculations]. The mechanism is high-coupon unsecured notes against a business whose margin is concentrated in offshore pipelines. The implication is that a modest EBITDA shortfall consumes interest cover quickly; the covenant minimum of 2.00x through December 31, 2026 rising to 2.15x in 2027 is not reported by management and cannot be tested here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth finding is covenant headroom. Management reports a covenant leverage ratio of 5.03x against a 5.75x maximum through December 31, 2027, and the release's own inputs imply an EBITDA cushion of USD 76.041 million or 12.5% [CP-1, Covenants and definitions review]. The mechanism is that covenant EBITDA includes pro forma adjustments of USD 11.405 million and covenant debt excludes the AR Facility; an illustrative fall of about 9.9% in computed EBITDA would lift computed leverage to 5.75x (Calculations; not a covenant test because the bases differ). The implication is that headroom is adequate today but is the variable that governs revolver access, and it cannot be verified without the executed credit agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fifth finding is business risk. Offshore pipelines produced 67.7% of nine-month 2026 Segment Margin under life-of-lease and minimum-volume arrangements, and in the third quarter Shenandoah volumes were below the minimum so only the minimum was recognized; management expects Adjusted EBITDA near or below the low end of guidance [CP-1A, Credit translations]. The mechanism is that minimum volume commitments floor margin but cap upside when third-party wells underperform, and Gulf weather adds interruption risk (about four days of disruption in October 2026). The implication is that the contracted base supports debt service while growth depends on producers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The sixth finding is cash conversion. Nine-month 2026 operating cash flow of USD 340.898 million included a working capital inflow of USD 58.619 million, and cash after capital payments and distributions was USD 101.661 million, before USD 221.594 million of preferred unit redemptions [CP-1, Credit narrative by dimension]. The mechanism is crude marketing, which moves receivables and payables together, with receivables partly financed through the AR Facility. The implication is that reported cash flow overstates the underlying run-rate and that free cash after distributions is small relative to debt, so deleveraging depends on EBITDA growth or asset sales rather than free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. First, contracted and fee-based offshore cash flow: pipelines under life-of-lease commitments and minimum volume commitments provided 67.7% of nine-month 2026 Segment Margin (Documentary Fact; CP-1A Company and operating model). Second, liquidity and maturity profile: USD 894.4 million of revolver availability, USD 41.477 million of cash and no maturity before January 2029 (Documentary Fact; CP-1). Third, diversified customers and assets: no customer above 10% of 2025 revenue, a marine fleet mostly on time charters and a sulfur services business with refinery contracts (Documentary Fact; CP-1A). Fourth, lower funding costs from the 2026 actions: the 2034 notes carry a lower coupon than the retired 2028 notes and the AR Facility prices at SOFR plus 1.375%, while repurchased preferred units carried an annual coupon of 11.24% (Documentary Fact; CP-1A Transaction summary). Management describes these steps as having eliminated near-term refinancing risk, which is Management Language and is not adopted here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. First, leverage and cover: 5.18x total debt to EBITDA and 2.36x EBITDA to cash interest, with debt higher than at year end (Documentary Fact for the figures; Analyst Interpretation for the reading). Second, earnings concentration and volume risk: offshore volumes depend on third-party producers, Shenandoah was at the minimum in Q3 2026 and management guides to the low end of the range (Documentary Fact; Management Language for the guidance). Third, control and capital allocation: Class B units elect the board and a family group holds 77% of them, and the partnership bought back preferred units with debt while raising common distributions (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation for the creditor reading). Fourth, definition and documentation gaps: the management covenant ratio uses a different debt and EBITDA perimeter and the executed credit documents are not supplied (Insufficient Information for covenant headroom verification).
